children: United Airlines reported higher third-quarter revenue, boosted by fare hikes, which helped to offset increased fuel costs stemming from the war in the Middle East.
The company reported net income of $1.03 billion, or $3.14 a share, up from $949 million, or $2.90 a share, the year prior.
Adjusted earnings were $2.54 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $2.57 a share.

Operating revenue jumped to $17.88 billion from $15.23 billion last year. Wall Street expected $17.89 billion. Revenue per available seat mile increased 16% from the previous year, while capacity increased 1.3%.
Aircraft fuel expenses rose to $4.84 billion from $3 billion in the prior-year period.

Earlier on Tuesday, oil prices rose above $111 a barrel before retreating slightly. Conflict in the Middle East has shown little sign of easing, constricting global oil supply and pushing up prices of jet fuel.
United has been able to offset most of its elevated fuel costs with higher fares, which haven't yet deterred travelers, the company said.
